0012-parser-robustness-format-tolerance..raw: **Problem 2 — QST placeholder matching**: The `[Fill this in]` pattern was too strict. `[ Fill this in  ]` (with spaces) didn't match, so the "write answer to file" logic fell back to inserting after the ANS header instead of replacing the placeholder. This caused double-answers on some questions. Also observed: the `- Status: unanswered` check is sensitive to whitespace and case.

**On placeholder matching**: `[Fill this in]` variants should be matched with a regex: `/^\[.*fill\s+this\s+in.*\]$/i`. This handles extra spaces, case variations, and surrounding text like `[ Fill this in ]` or `[fill this in please]`.
Also handle `[ Fill this in  ]` by trimming around the brackets:

**D9.4 — NONSTANDARD_FILL_PLACEHOLDER** (bracket-form variants). Specimens: `[see hand drawing — pending]` ([temp/misc-problem-adr-05/0006-buffon-node-visual-vocabulary.md:73](../../temp/misc-problem-adr-05/0006-buffon-node-visual-vocabulary.md)), `[awaiting]` ([temp/misc-problem-adr-05/0007-etude-ui-evolution.md:114-115](../../temp/misc-problem-adr-05/0007-etude-ui-evolution.md)), and `**ANS:** (by )` with empty author parens and no body ([temp/misc-problem-adr-05/0004-alternative-flight-data-sources.md:300-301](../../temp/misc-problem-adr-05/0004-alternative-flight-data-sources.md)). Fix: broaden the placeholder regex family to `/^\[\s*(fill\s+this\s+in|awaiting|pending|tbd|see\s+.+|to\s+fill)[^\]]*\]$/i` and treat `**ANS:** (by *)` followed by blank/EOF as an implicit placeholder. Pair with the ANS-finder hardening (R4 was in Iteration 1 of the master-plan seed).

DEBRIEF-003-panel-background-refresh-clo.raw: **A second, unrelated bug was found and fixed in the same session**: the exact `[ ]` (bare empty-bracket) placeholder Jérémie used in a real file (`temp/0048-mcp-support-rfc-connecting-external-tool-servers.md`) wasn't recognized by the parser's placeholder-tolerance regex (`PLACEHOLDER_SYNONYM_RE`, which only covered named tokens like `[unanswered]`, `[tbd]`, etc. — the D9.4 class). A bare `[ ]` became a literal "answer," and the question silently vanished from the panel as done. This is the same failure class as D9.4's original specimen, just a token D9.4 didn't cover yet — fixed with a dedicated `PLACEHOLDER_EMPTY_RE`, deliberately kept separate from the synonym regex rather than folded in, to avoid accidentally widening it to match *any* bracketed text (which would misread a real answer like `"[see ADR-0014]"` as a placeholder).

4. **D9.4's placeholder tolerance is a token list, not a closed set — treat every new gap as an expected instance of the same class, not a new bug.** This is the second specimen (`[unanswered]`, now `[ ]`) found in real usage within two days. The class isn't closed; the next gap is a matter of when, not if.
